Upper bounds — holds for every partial

  • \(\mathrm{PostQ}_\varepsilon(f) = \Theta(\mathrm{rdeg}_\varepsilon(f))\)
    MahadevdeWolf15
    Post-selected quantum query complexity is characterised by approximate rational degree, exactly as $\mathrm{Q}$ is characterised (polynomially) by approximate degree. Rational degree is defined with no boundedness required off the domain, and the implementation direction rescales $p$ and $q$ jointly, which leaves $p/q$ fixed -- so the characterisation is a partial-function one.

This is the reason rational degree is in the zoo at all: it is the natural "$\mathsf{PostBQP}$" analogue of $\widetilde{\deg}$. Its exact version $\mathrm{rdeg}$ -- equivalently $\mathrm{PostQ}_{\mathrm{E}}$, zero-error post-selected quantum query complexity -- is the one Fortnow asked about, answered in [KKWY26].
